full_judgment:
Mr. Bijan Kumar Das, J: This appeal arises against judgment and order dated 29.4.93 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Naogon refusing to re-admit the appeal under order 41 rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure in Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 1992. The present appellant filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1988 before the learned District Judge, Naogaon against the judgment and decree dismissing the suit for declaration of title to the suit land. The appeal was ultimately fixed for hearing on 3.5.92 when an application for adjournment was filed on behalf of the appellant but it was not pressed and the Sub ordinate judge. (now Joint District Judge) dismissed the appeal for default on 3.5.1992. The appellant as petitioner then field Miscellaneous Case No. 77 of 2002 under Order 41 rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure for re-admission of the appeal. The appellant was examined and on consideration of her evidence and the materials on record the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) found no sufficient cause was proved by the appellant to re-admit the appeal. Accordingly by judgment and order dated 29.4.93 learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the miscellaneous case. 

 3. Mr. S. N. Goswami, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellant has taken me through the impugned order and all other connected papers including an affidavit sworn by the learned Advocate Mr. Joynal Abedin (Minto). Mr. Goswami submits that Mr. Joynal Abedin (Minto), the learned Advocate engaged by the appellant and he was empowered to exercise all the powers to conduct the appeal before the learned lower appellate court and the learned Advocate Mr. Joynal Abedin (Minto) himself appeared by swearing an affidavit stating that he was ill in his village home and a clerk from his chamber made a prayer for adjournment before the learned Subordinate Judge which was rejected and the appeal was dismissed. It is submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge could have allowed the case under order 41 rule 19 C.P.C. upon awarding some cost as provided under the law but dismissal of the appeal has caused irreparable loss and injury to the illiterate village lady and in such case the courts should, decide the matter taking lenient view. This was not done in the present case. No one has entered appearance on behalf of the respondents despite service of notice on the respondents. 

 4. I have perused the impugned order and the evidence on record including the affidavit sworn by the learned Advocate Mr. Md. Joinul Abedin (Minto). It appears that the learned Advocate Mr. Joynul Abedin (Minto) in his affidavit admitted that he was engaged as the learned Advocate to conduct the case on behalf of the appellant and that he was entrusted to exercise all the powers which were necessary for the purpose of conducting the appeal. The learned Advocate has stated being an advocate engaged on behalf of the appellant that the learned Subordinate Judge was not correct in holding that the appellant could not prove that Mr. Joinal Abedin was not an engaged learned Advocate of the appellant. Further, in view of the averment made in the affidavit by the learned Advocate Mr. Joinal Abedin (Minto) that he fell sick on 3.5.1992 in his village home I do not find any reason to disbelieve his statement. The learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) committed an error of fact in holding that the appellant could not prove that the said learned Advocate Mr. Joinal Abedin (Minto) was ill on 3.5.92. The affidavit filed by the learned member of the bar should not be totally ignored or lightly brushed side by the court but should consider the statements made in such affidavit for a correct adjudication of the issue involved in the suit or in the appeal. In the facts of the case I am of the view that the appellant should be given an opportunity to press the appeal on merit but not without any cost. 

 6. In the result this appeal is allowed with cost. The impugned judgment and order dated 29.4.93 passed by the then Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Naogaon in Miscellaneous Case No.77 of 2002 under order 41 rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure is hereby set aside and Title Appeal No. 50 of 1988 is restored to its file and number on condition of payment of cost of Tk. 2000/- by the appellant to the respondents within a period of 3(three) months from the date of the receipt of the records by the lower appellate court.
